## MoRIIOConnector Overview

MoRIIOConnector is a high-performance KV connector used for KV cache transfer in PD disaggregated deployments, built on ROCm's MoRI-IO communication library for point-to-point communication with ultra-low overhead. It was added to vLLM as part of ROCm/PD support work.

## KV Cache Handoff and Transfer Modes

Under the hood, MORI-IO (exposed in vLLM as the MoRIIOConnector) manages the KV-cache handoff. Regardless of transfer mode, before the first RDMA transfer between an instance pair, MORI-IO performs a one-time metadata exchange via ZMQ. MORI-IO supports two transfer modes that differ in who initiates the RDMA transfer and how the proxy orchestrates the two phases.

The mode is controlled via an environment variable: The mode is set by the VLLM_MORIIO_CONNECTOR_READ_MODE environment variable.

**Read mode:** In read mode, the proxy dispatches to prefill and decode serially: it waits for prefill to complete, extracts the remote block IDs, then forwards them to decode. The decode instance uses those IDs to pull the KV cache from prefill via RDMA.

**Write mode:** In write mode, the proxy dispatches to prefill and decode concurrently — without waiting for prefill to finish first. The prefill instance pushes the KV cache layer-by-layer directly into the decode instance's pre-allocated memory as it computes each layer. Specifically, as each layer is computed, save_kv_layer issues an RDMA write directly into the decode instance's pre-allocated KV block memory.

## Metadata Handshake

Before the first RDMA transfer between an instance pair, MORI-IO performs a one-time metadata exchange via ZMQ — sharing KV cache base addresses, block sizes, and per-layer tensor strides. This handshake runs asynchronously in a background thread so it doesn't block the engine loop, and the resulting RDMA session is cached for all subsequent requests. Both modes share the same handshake and RDMA transport — the differences are entirely at the proxy dispatch layer and the direction of the transfer.

## Engine Internals

The MoRIIO engine wrapper handles the transfer roles: it wraps MoRIIO engine operations and handles both producer and consumer roles for KV cache transfers. It handles write operations for KV cache transfers and implements distributed KV cache transfer using the MoRIIO library for RDMA-based communication between prefill and decode instances. The write worker uses a transfer plan structure — _prepare_transfer_plan takes a WriteTask, RemoteAllocInfo, and MoRIIOAgentMetadata and returns a LayerTransferPlan.

For same-host deployments: use xGMI when the prefiller and decoder run on the same physical host so transfers go over the AMD GPU fabric and skip the NIC entirely.
